_comments: Registry of external agent harnesses this installation can launch. A row makes a harness
AVAILABLE; an agent opts in by naming it in AIAgent.TypeConfiguration ({ "harnessName": ... }).
STATUS is 'Inactive' for every row by default. These harnesses are external binaries that must
be installed and authenticated on whatever host (or in whatever sandbox image) will run them,
so shipping them Active would mean a fresh install advertises harnesses it cannot launch.
Flip a row to Active once its binary is present.
CapabilitySettings declares what each ADAPTER implements, not what the vendor advertises — the
runtime emulates what is missing, so an over-claim becomes a silent behavioural gap.
PermissionPolicy vs PermissionHooks are different questions and were once conflated:
· PermissionPolicy — the adapter translates MJ's posture and allow/deny lists into flags the
harness honours. FALSE means a configured policy is INERT and the runtime logs an error.
True only for Claude Code and Pi, whose flags were verified against real installs; the
others stay false until someone verifies theirs rather than guessing.
· PermissionHooks — the adapter can intercept a permission prompt mid-turn and route it to a
human. False everywhere: MJ's MCP permission-prompt tool does not exist yet.
Note on Claude Code's Bash patterns: they are PREFIX-LITERAL, so `Bash(git commit:*)` does not
match `git -C <path> commit`. Deny whole tool names; do not try to carve subcommands out of a
broad allow. Real containment comes from the sandbox provider.

fields.Name: Claude Code
fields.Description: Anthropic's Claude Code, driven through its headless CLI (`claude -p --output-format stream-json`). Resumes sessions natively, so context stays server-side rather than being replayed each turn. Requires the `claude` binary on PATH (or set ExecutablePath) and an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY reaching the sandbox via MJ: AI Agent Credentials.

fields.Name: Codex CLI
fields.Description: OpenAI's Codex CLI, driven through `codex exec --json`. Ships as a CLI only — the npm package exposes a bin and no library entry point. Requires the `codex` binary and an OPENAI_API_KEY reaching the sandbox.

fields.Name: OpenCode
fields.Description: OpenCode in non-interactive run mode. The published @opencode-ai/sdk exposes no main or types entry, so the CLI is the dependable contract. Requires the `opencode` binary.

fields.Name: Gemini CLI
fields.Description: Google's Gemini CLI. Built around one-shot invocations, so it does NOT resume sessions — the runtime replays accumulated context into every turn and budgets the extra tokens against the run's guardrails. Uses the CLI rather than @google/gemini-cli-core, which is internals with no stability contract. Requires the `gemini` binary and a GEMINI_API_KEY.

fields.Name: Pi
fields.Description: Pi (@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent), driven through its non-interactive CLI: `pi -p --mode json --session-id <id>`. Verified against a real install (0.83.0) rather than inferred — MJ supplies the session id up front, so turns resume instead of replaying context. Authenticates from environment variables or its own `pi /login`; the local executor passes HOME through, so a developer who has already logged in needs no credential row.
